definition: The basic unit of text that a language model processes, which may be a word, part of a word, or punctuation mark, produced by a tokenizer.
details: Language models don't operate directly on raw text; they operate on sequences of token IDs. The choice of tokenization scheme affects vocabulary size, sequence length, and how efficiently the model represents rare words.
story: Picture an architect laying out a building where every room has to know which other rooms matter to it. Boil it down and it is this: The basic unit of text that a language model processes, which may be a word, part of a word, or punctuation mark, produced by a tokenizer. Here is why it matters: Language models don't operate directly on raw text; they operate on sequences of token IDs. It is the difference between a row of isolated cubicles and one big room where everyone can hear each other. That blueprint is Token.
